paper.title: Stochastic Contextual Dueling Bandits under Linear Stochastic Transitivity Models

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual dueling bandits under (contextualized) linear stochastic transitivity models (CoLST)
unmapped: Comparison function F* (link) is known to the learner; derivative of F* is L-Lipschitz and bounded below by mu > 0 near theta* (Assumption A2)
the learner knows mu (lower bound on F*' ) and rho (minimum eigenvalue of the spanning basis of contexts) to set tau and c1
context vectors in the unit l2 ball and contain a basis with sum b_j b_j^T >= rho I_d at each round (A1)
regret measured as average regret (mean utility gap of both selected arms) w.r.t. the per-context best-utility arm
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the feedback is generated by means of a CoLST model with a known perturbation distribution G^* (and corresponding comparison function F^*) and an unknown weight parameter theta^*. ... P(Y_t = 1 | Z_t) = F^*( <z_{t,i_t,j_t}, theta^*> )

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual dueling bandits under linear stochastic transitivity models (lower bound)
unmapped: regret is weak regret: utility gap of the better of the two selected arms w.r.t. the per-context best arm
settings.definition_quote: For any learning algorithm A for the contextual dueling bandits problem under linear stochastic transitivity models in dimension d, there exists an instance of the problem characterized by a weight vector theta^* in B_1(2), context space X subseteq B_1(infty), and a comparison function F

conditions: context space X subseteq B_1(infty) (construction uses {-1,1}^d)
BTL comparison function in hard instance

source.label: theorem:lower_bound_weak_regret
source.quote: For any learning algorithm $\cA$ ... there exists an instance of the problem characterized by a weight vector $\btheta^* \in \cB_1(2)$, context space $\X \subseteq \cB_1(\infty),$ and a comparison function $F$, such that the expected weak regret incurred by $\cA$ in any $T > \max(d,16)$ rounds is $\mathbb{E}[R_T^w]=\Omega(d\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Bound on expected weak regret (defined via utilities, so pseudo-regret type). Also lower bounds average regret since R^w <= R^a.

conditions: BTL comparison function in hard instance

source.label: theorem:lower_bound_weak_regret
source.quote: Further, if we restrict $\X \subseteq \cB_1(2)$, then $\mathbb{E} \big[ R_T^w((S_t^\cA)_{t\in[T]}) \big] = \Omega\big(\sqrt{dT}\big).$

results.notes: Weak regret lower bound with unit-l2 contexts.

conditions: Assumption A1: contexts in unit l2 ball and contain a basis with sum b_j b_j^T >= rho I_d
Assumption A2: F*' is L-Lipschitz and mu = inf F*'(x^T theta) > 0 over ||x||<=2, ||theta-theta*||<=1
tuning: c_1 = (1/(2 mu)) sqrt(d log(T/d) + 2 log T)
tau = d + max{d^2 log(T)/(mu^2 rho), d/rho}
p_t = min(1, sqrt(2d)/(2 sqrt(t-tau)) (3 c_1 + c_2) sqrt(log(2T/d)))

source.label: theorem_regret_bound
source.quote: Let $c_1= \frac{1}{2\mu}\sqrt{d \log(T/d) +2\log(T)}$ and $\tau=d + \max\{ d^2 \log(T)/(\mu^2 \rho) ,d/\rho \}.$ ... For any $ C_{\mathrm{thresh}} \in(0,c_2)$, it holds that the expected cumulative average regret of CoLSTIM is in $O(d\sqrt{T}\log(T))$ for any CoLST model with weight vector $\btheta^*$ such that $\|\btheta^*\|\in \cB_1(2)$ and comparison function $F^*$ satisfying assumption (A2), and any $(\bX_t)_{t\in[T]}$ satisfying assumption (A1).

results.notes: Expected cumulative average regret (utility-based), recorded as pseudo-regret. Hidden constants depend on mu, rho. Derived from general Theorem C.1 (not recorded separately).

conditions: Assumptions A1 and A2 as in Theorem 3.2
sum_{t=tau+1}^T lambda_min^{-1/2}(M_t) <= c sqrt(T) for some constant c > 0

source.label: corollary_colstim
source.quote: Under the assumptions of Theorem \ref{theorem_regret_bound} and if $\sum_{t=\tau+1}^T \lambda_{\min}^{-1/2}(\bM_t)\leq c \sqrt{T},$ ... the expected cumulative average regret of CoLSTIM is in $O( \sqrt{dT}\log(T)).$

results.notes: Eigenvalue condition is on the algorithm's Gram matrix (satisfied for dense contexts per the paper).

conditions: Assumptions A1 and A2 as in Theorem 3.2
tuning: c_1 = (3/(2 mu)) sqrt(2 log(3 n T^2))

source.label: theorem_regret_bound_Sup_colstim
source.quote: Let $c_1= \frac{3}{2\mu}\sqrt{2 \log( 3 n T^2)}$ and $\tau$ as in Theorem \ref{theorem_regret_bound}. ... it holds for any $ C_{\mathrm{thresh}} < c_2$ that the expected cumulative average regret of Sup-CoLSTIM is in $O(\sqrt{dT\log(n)}\log^{3/2}(T)).$

results.notes: Paper's n (number of arms) mapped to K.
